reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a highly regular, piecewise-linear quasi-periodic waveform with a fundamental period of 55 points (confirmed by metadata and visual cycle counting). Each cycle consists of a sharp, near-symmetric triangular rise (≈15–20 points) to a single peak, followed by a slower, multi-step descent (≈30–35 points) with 3–4 flat or gently sloping plateaus. Peaks consistently reach robust-standardized values between 1.7 and 2.2; troughs stabilize near −0.5 to −1.0, often holding a flat segment for 5–10 points. Baseline level varies modestly across candidates (median from −0.22 to +0.44), but the *shape*—rise steepness, plateau count/length, descent step size—is conserved. Noise is negligible: all segments are linear or constant (roughness ≈ 0), indicating quantization or discretized control. Amplitude (90th percentile) ranges 2.5–3.0, reflecting minor scaling shifts rather than structural change. No sustained trend per cycle; slope_per_point is near-zero (<±0.014), though small drifts appear over longer windows due to baseline shifts. Boundary truncation is minimal: all candidates start/end mid-descent or on a plateau, preserving full-cycle morphology. Acceptable variation includes ±0.2 in peak height, ±0.1 in trough depth, and ±2 points in rise/descent duration—provided the 3–4 plateau structure remains intact.
